data.title: CSV export — backend/frontend integration points
data.description:
## Parent Ideation Context
- Title: CSV export for filtered issue views
- Version: 17

### Description
Users need to export the issues currently visible in an Issues List view — respecting whatever filters/sort are active — as a CSV file, for reporting and sharing outside Plane. Real, commonly-requested feature across project-management tools. Backend: new DRF endpoint honoring the same filter/sort params as the existing issue-list endpoint, small result sets return CSV synchronously, large ones queue a Celery job and return a signed download link, respecting project member view permissions. Frontend: an Export action on the Issues List view, filter-aware, with toast/progress state and polling for async exports.

### Problem Statement
Users viewing a filtered/sorted Issues List in Plane have no way to get that exact view out of the app as a file. They currently resort to manual copy-paste or third-party scraping to share issue data with stakeholders who don't have Plane access, or to build reports outside the tool. This is a gap versus comparable project-management tools, which almost universally offer list export.

Scope is bounded to CSV export of the Issues List view, respecting whatever filter/sort state is currently applied — not a general data-export/reporting feature, not other entity types (cycles, modules, pages), and not other formats (XLSX, PDF) for v1.

### Proposed Approach
Backend (apps/api): new `GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/projects/<id>/issues/export/` endpoint reusing the existing issue-list endpoint's filter/sort query-param handling and project-member view permissions (no exporting issues a role can't see).

- Sync/async split at a **500-issue** ceiling (resolved via Q&A: conservative choice, favors sync-path latency safety over minimizing async volume). Below 500 matched issues, the CSV streams back synchronously in the response. At or above 500, the request queues a Celery job (matching Plane's existing async job patterns) and returns a signed download link.
- CSV columns are a **fixed core set** (resolved via Q&A: ID, title, status, priority, assignee, labels, due date, created/updated) — not view-configuration-dependent, not a full field superset. Predictable schema for both the serializer and any downstream tooling parsing the file.
- Signed download links expire after **24 hours** (resolved via Q&A: more forgiving than Plane's existing 1-hour SIGNED_URL_EXPIRATION default for other signed links, since a queued export may sit before the user returns to download it; accepted tradeoff of a longer exposure window for v1).

Frontend (apps/web): filter-aware "Export" action on the Issues List view — exports exactly what's currently on screen. Sync path triggers an immediate file download; async path shows toast + progress state and polls for the signed link, then prompts download.

Test/Validator card: backend pytest coverage across filter combinations and permission boundaries; frontend Playwright test for the export flow (both sync and async paths); validator confirms both against the spec's acceptance criteria before the card is marked done.

### Scope Assessment
- Domains: 2/5
- Ambiguity: 2/5
- Dependencies: 1/5
- Complexity: medium

## Refinement Description
## Parent Ideation Context
- Title: CSV export for filtered issue views
- Version: 17

### Description
Users need to export the issues currently visible in an Issues List view — respecting whatever filters/sort are active — as a CSV file, for reporting and sharing outside Plane. Real, commonly-requested feature across project-management tools. Backend: new DRF endpoint honoring the same filter/sort params as the existing issue-list endpoint, small result sets return CSV synchronously, large ones queue a Celery job and return a signed download link, respecting project member view permissions. Frontend: an Export action on the Issues List view, filter-aware, with toast/progress state and polling for async exports.

### Problem Statement
Users viewing a filtered/sorted Issues List in Plane have no way to get that exact view out of the app as a file. They currently resort to manual copy-paste or third-party scraping to share issue data with stakeholders who don't have Plane access, or to build reports outside the tool. This is a gap versus comparable project-management tools, which almost universally offer list export.

Scope is bounded to CSV export of the Issues List view, respecting whatever filter/sort state is currently applied — not a general data-export/reporting feature, not other entity types (cycles, modules, pages), and not other formats (XLSX, PDF) for v1.

### Proposed Approach
Backend (apps/api): new `GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/projects/<id>/issues/export/` endpoint reusing the existing issue-list endpoint's filter/sort query-param handling and project-member view permissions (no exporting issues a role can't see).

- Sync/async split at a **500-issue** ceiling (resolved via Q&A: conservative choice, favors sync-path latency safety over minimizing async volume). Below 500 matched issues, the CSV streams back synchronously in the response. At or above 500, the request queues a Celery job (matching Plane's existing async job patterns) and returns a signed download link.
- CSV columns are a **fixed core set** (resolved via Q&A: ID, title, status, priority, assignee, labels, due date, created/updated) — not view-configuration-dependent, not a full field superset. Predictable schema for both the serializer and any downstream tooling parsing the file.
- Signed download links expire after **24 hours** (resolved via Q&A: more forgiving than Plane's existing 1-hour SIGNED_URL_EXPIRATION default for other signed links, since a queued export may sit before the user returns to download it; accepted tradeoff of a longer exposure window for v1).

Frontend (apps/web): filter-aware "Export" action on the Issues List view — exports exactly what's currently on screen. Sync path triggers an immediate file download; async path shows toast + progress state and polls for the signed link, then prompts download.

Test/Validator card: backend pytest coverage across filter combinations and permission boundaries; frontend Playwright test for the export flow (both sync and async paths); validator confirms both against the spec's acceptance criteria before the card is marked done.

### Scope Assessment
- Domains: 2/5
- Ambiguity: 2/5
- Dependencies: 1/5
- Complexity: medium

## In Scope
- Extend ExportIssuesEndpoint / issue_export_task to accept and apply the Issues List view's active filter/sort state via the existing (currently unused) ExporterHistory.rich_filters field
- Export action on the IssuesHeader toolbar (apps/web/core/components/issues/header.tsx, Header.RightItem), filter-aware, reusing the existing ExportForm/PrevExports toast+polling UX pattern
- Reuse existing IssueExportSerializer column set as-is (no new serializer)
- Reuse existing always-async ExportIssuesEndpoint/Celery/7-day-signed-URL pattern as-is (no new sync path, no new expiry policy)
- Permission scoping consistent with the existing exporter's WORKSPACE-level role check

## Out of Scope
- A new/separate export endpoint independent of the existing ExportIssuesEndpoint
- A new CSV column set or new serializer
- A new synchronous (non-Celery) export path
- A new signed-URL expiry policy
- Other entity types (cycles, modules, pages)
- Other export formats beyond what the existing exporter already supports (it already supports XLSX/JSON alongside CSV — no new format work needed)
- Configurable CSV column selection

## Analysis
Investigated the actual `okto-plane-handoff-demo/plane` fork (branch `feature/issue-csv-export`, forked from `makeplane/plane`) before assuming any new endpoint was needed. Key finding: **Plane already ships a complete CSV/XLSX/JSON export system** — this is not a greenfield addition, it is an extension of existing, working infrastructure.

**Existing async export pipeline (evidence:plane-repo, brownfield delivered behavior):**
- `ExportIssuesEndpoint` (`apps/api/plane/app/views/exporter/base.py:18-79`) — `POST /workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/`, `@allow_permission([ROLE.ADMIN, ROLE.MEMBER], level="WORKSPACE")`. Creates an `ExporterHistory` row (`status="queued"`), calls `issue_export_task.delay(...)`, returns immediately. `GET` on the same endpoint lists `ExporterHistory` for polling.
- `issue_export_task` (`apps/api/plane/bgtasks/export_task.py:127-226`, `@shared_task`) — builds the `Issue` queryset with the same membership/role scoping as the list endpoints, serializes via `DataExporter(IssueExportSerializer, format_type=provider)`, zips, uploads, sets `status="completed"`/`"failed"`.
- `upload_to_s3` (`export_task.py:42-124`) — generates the presigned download URL via boto3 `generate_presigned_url`, `ExpiresIn = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60` (**7 days** — an established, already-used convention, not the 24h this refinement's parent ideation assumed before this investigation).
- `ExporterHistory` model (`apps/api/plane/db/models/exporter.py:24-63`) already has a `status` state machine (`queued|processing|completed|failed`), `provider`, `url`, `key`, and — notably — a `filters`/`rich_filters` JSONField that is **present on the model but unused**: `ExportForm` (`apps/web/core/components/exporter/export-form.tsx:216-248`) has a `WorkspaceLevelWorkItemFiltersHOC` block stubbed out/commented, meaning Plane's own developers scaffolded filter-aware export but never wired it up.
- `IssueExportSerializer` (`apps/api/plane/utils/porters/serializers/issue.py:12-63+`) is already a rich, human-readable export shape: `identifier`, `project_name`, `project_identifier`, `state_name`, `priority`, `assignees` (names), `labels` (names), dates, `estimate`, `cycles`, `modules`, `sub_issues_count` — richer than any new fixed column set would be, and already CSV-wired via `DataExporter`.
- Frontend UX pattern already exists end-to-end: `ExportForm` (`export-form.tsx:100-138`) fires the job and shows a toast ("Once the export is ready you will be able to download it") via `@plane/propel/toast`; `PrevExports` (`apps/web/core/components/exporter/prev-exports.tsx:49-74`) polls the `ExporterHistory` list every 3000ms via `setInterval` while any row is `processing`, with a manual "Refresh status" fallback.
- Confirmed no separate/newer async-job abstraction exists elsewhere in `apps/web` — the exporter feature is the only polling-based async-job pattern in the codebase (explicit non-finding, not an assumption).

**Toolbar integration point:** `IssuesHeader` (`apps/web/core/components/issues/header.tsx:35-131`), specifically `Header.RightItem` (lines 107-127) where `HeaderFilters` and the "Add work item" button already live — this is shared across all Issues List layouts (list/spreadsheet/kanban), so a new Export action placed there appears regardless of active layout.

**Decision reconciliation (see `decisions` — this refinement corrects three assumptions frozen in the parent ideation's `done` snapshot, per user confirmation):** the ideation's sync/async 500-issue threshold, 24h signed-URL expiry, and fixed-core-column-set decisions were made without knowledge of the existing exporter; on discovering the contradiction, the choice was surfaced to the user rather than silently overridden, and the user chose to adopt Plane's existing conventions in all three cases. This ideation is superseded by, not contradicted by, this refinement — the underlying goal (filter-aware CSV export from the Issues List view) is unchanged; only the implementation strategy shifted from "build new" to "extend existing."

## Decisions
- SUPERSEDES ideation decision (sync/async 500-issue threshold): adopt Plane's existing always-async ExportIssuesEndpoint/issue_export_task pattern instead of building a new synchronous fast path. Alternatives considered: keep the new sync path as originally decided (rejected — would duplicate/diverge from an established, working async convention for no clear user benefit; a small export still completes in seconds via the existing 3s-interval poll). Source: apps/api/plane/app/views/exporter/base.py:18-79, apps/api/plane/bgtasks/export_task.py:127-226. User confirmed via Q&A.
- SUPERSEDES ideation decision (24h signed-URL expiry): adopt the existing 7-day presigned-URL expiry (upload_to_s3, export_task.py:47,75-79,108-112) instead of a new 24h value. Alternatives considered: keep 24h as a tighter security window (rejected — introduces an inconsistent expiry policy across the app's export surfaces for a link that already reuses the same S3/MinIO bucket and permission model). User confirmed via Q&A.
- SUPERSEDES ideation decision (fixed core CSV column set): reuse the existing IssueExportSerializer (apps/api/plane/utils/porters/serializers/issue.py:12-63+) instead of authoring a new narrower serializer. Alternatives considered: the ideation's fixed core set of 8 fields (rejected — the existing serializer already ships a richer, human-readable shape wired to CSV; building a narrower one would be duplicate serialization code for less information). User confirmed via Q&A.
- NEW decision: the feature's real scope is wiring the existing ExportIssuesEndpoint/issue_export_task to accept and apply the Issues List view's active filter/sort state via the already-present-but-unused ExporterHistory.rich_filters field, plus adding an Export action to IssuesHeader's Header.RightItem (apps/web/core/components/issues/header.tsx:107-127) that calls it, rather than building an independent new endpoint. Alternatives considered: a wholly separate view-scoped endpoint (rejected — apps/web/core/components/exporter/export-form.tsx already stubs a WorkspaceLevelWorkItemFiltersHOC block for exactly this integration, indicating Plane's own team intended this exact extension path). User confirmed via Q&A.

functional_requirements.text: The workspace export endpoint (POST /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/, ExportIssuesEndpoint) accepts an optional `rich_filters` object in the request body mirroring the Issues List view's active filter/sort state (project_id, IssueFilterSet-compatible filter fields, order_by); when present, issue_export_task applies these filters to the Issue queryset before serialization, in addition to the existing membership/role scoping.
When `rich_filters` is omitted from the request, the endpoint behaves exactly as it does today (full workspace export) — fully backward compatible with existing callers of ExportIssuesEndpoint.

The ExporterHistory row persists the submitted `rich_filters` verbatim in its existing `rich_filters` JSONField for audit/replay, using the field that already exists on the model but is currently never populated.

The Issues List toolbar (IssuesHeader component, Header.RightItem section) renders an 'Export CSV' action, visible only to a user whose role satisfies the existing exporter's WORKSPACE-level role check (ROLE.ADMIN or ROLE.MEMBER).

Clicking the Export CSV action submits a POST to /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ with provider='csv' and a `rich_filters` payload built from the current Issues List view's active project, filter, and sort state.
On submission, the frontend shows a toast confirming the export was queued, reusing the existing ExportForm success-toast pattern (@plane/propel/toast).
The frontend polls the ExporterHistory list via the existing PrevExports interval mechanism and surfaces a download action once the matching entry's status becomes 'completed'.
If the matching export job's status becomes 'failed', the frontend surfaces the failure via a distinct error/toast state rather than continuing to poll indefinitely.

technical_requirements.text: `rich_filters` MUST be validated server-side against the same filter vocabulary as `IssueFilterSet` (apps/api/plane/utils/filters/filterset.py) — an unrecognized filter key is rejected with HTTP 400, never silently ignored, to prevent a silently-wrong export.

`issue_export_task` MUST apply `rich_filters` via the same ComplexFilterBackend/`IssueFilterSet`-compatible queryset construction already used by `IssueListEndpoint` (apps/api/plane/app/views/issue/base.py:80-205) — not a parallel/duplicate filter implementation — so filter semantics never drift between the live Issues List view and its export.

The existing membership/role scoping already present in `issue_export_task` (project__project_projectmember__member=..., is_active=True) remains the outer bound on every export: `rich_filters` may narrow the exported set but must never be capable of expanding it beyond what the requesting user's role can already view.

No change to `upload_to_s3`'s presigned-URL expiry (7 days, export_task.py:47,75-79,108-112) or to `IssueExportSerializer`'s field set (apps/api/plane/utils/porters/serializers/issue.py:12-63+) — per the refinement's superseding decision, this feature only adds filter application to the existing pipeline, not new serialization or storage code.

The Export button's visible/disabled state on the frontend MUST be derived from the same role/permission data the Issues List toolbar already uses for the adjacent 'Add work item' button (apps/web/core/components/issues/header.tsx:107-127) — not a new, separately-maintained permission check.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an Issues List view with an active filter (e.g. status = In Progress) and a chosen sort order, when the user clicks Export CSV, then the downloaded CSV contains only issues matching that filter, in the chosen sort order, and contains zero issues outside the filter.
Given a user whose role has no view access to a project's issues, when that project's Issues List is rendered, then the Export CSV action is not rendered or is disabled for that project.

Given a rich_filters payload containing an unrecognized filter key, when the export request is submitted, then the server responds HTTP 400 with a structured error identifying the invalid key, and no ExporterHistory row transitions past 'queued'.

Given an export job that reaches status='completed', when the frontend's next poll observes it, then the UI displays a working download action that resolves to the CSV via the existing 7-day presigned URL.
Given an export job that reaches status='failed', when the frontend's next poll observes it, then the UI displays a failure indication visibly distinct from the in-progress/polling state.

Given a request to POST /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ with no rich_filters field (a legacy caller), when processed, then the endpoint's behavior is identical to its pre-feature behavior (full workspace export, no regression).

test_scenarios.title: Export respects active filter and sort
test_scenarios.given: A project with 10 issues, 4 of which have priority=urgent, and an Issues List view with filter priority=urgent and sort=-created_at active
test_scenarios.then: The completed export's CSV contains exactly the 4 urgent issues, ordered by created_at descending, and zero non-urgent issues

test_scenarios.title: Export action hidden for a role without view access
test_scenarios.given: A user whose workspace role does not satisfy ROLE.ADMIN or ROLE.MEMBER for the target project
test_scenarios.when: That user's Issues List view for the project is rendered
test_scenarios.then: The Export CSV action is not present in Header.RightItem (or is rendered disabled), matching the visibility of the existing 'Add work item' button

test_scenarios.title: Unrecognized filter key rejects the request
test_scenarios.given: A POST to /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ with rich_filters.filters containing the key "not_a_real_filter"
test_scenarios.then: The server responds HTTP 400 with error=invalid_filter_key naming "not_a_real_filter", and no ExporterHistory row advances past status=queued for this request

test_scenarios.title: Completed export surfaces a working download link
test_scenarios.given: An export job in status=processing that the frontend is polling via the existing PrevExports interval
test_scenarios.when: The job transitions to status=completed with a presigned url set
test_scenarios.then: The next poll surfaces a download action in the UI, and following it downloads the CSV via the presigned URL before its 7-day expiry

test_scenarios.title: Failed export surfaces a distinct error state
test_scenarios.given: An export job in status=processing that the frontend is polling
test_scenarios.then: The next poll surfaces a failure indication in the UI that is visually and textually distinct from the processing/spinner state, and polling for that job stops

test_scenarios.title: Legacy request without rich_filters is unaffected
test_scenarios.given: The existing workspace-level ExportForm submits a POST to /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ with no rich_filters field, exactly as it does today
test_scenarios.when: The request is processed by the modified endpoint and issue_export_task
test_scenarios.then: The resulting export contains the full workspace issue set exactly as it would have before this feature shipped — no regression

business_rules.title: rich_filters can only narrow the exported set, never widen it
business_rules.rule: The exported issue set after applying rich_filters must always be a subset of the issues the requesting user's role already has view access to, computed by the existing membership/role scoping in issue_export_task
business_rules.when: A request to POST /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ includes a rich_filters payload
business_rules.then: issue_export_task applies rich_filters as an additional AND-ed constraint on top of the existing role-scoped queryset, never as a replacement for it or an independent filter that could bypass role scoping
business_rules.notes: Prevents a maliciously or accidentally crafted rich_filters payload from exporting issues the user cannot otherwise see. Source: apps/api/plane/bgtasks/export_task.py existing role-scoping queryset.

business_rules.title: Unknown filter keys reject the request rather than degrading silently
business_rules.rule: The server must not silently drop, ignore, or apply a best-effort interpretation of an unrecognized filter key
business_rules.when: rich_filters contains one or more keys that are not part of the IssueFilterSet-compatible filter vocabulary
business_rules.then: The endpoint responds HTTP 400 with a structured error identifying the invalid key(s), and no ExporterHistory row is created or advances past queued for that request
business_rules.notes: A silently-ignored filter key would produce an export that looks correct but is silently wrong (exports more than the user intended) — fail closed instead.

business_rules.title: Omitting rich_filters is fully backward compatible
business_rules.rule: The absence of rich_filters must never be interpreted as an empty/zero-match filter
business_rules.when: A request to POST /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ has no rich_filters field at all (legacy caller / existing ExportForm workspace-level export)
business_rules.then: The endpoint and issue_export_task behave exactly as they did before this feature — full workspace export, no behavioral regression for existing callers
business_rules.notes: Protects the existing ExportForm workspace-level export flow, which will continue calling this endpoint without rich_filters.

business_rules.title: Export button visibility mirrors the existing 'Add work item' permission check
business_rules.rule: The Export CSV action must not introduce a second, independently-maintained permission check that could drift from the existing role check
business_rules.when: The Issues List toolbar (Header.RightItem) is rendered for a given user and project
business_rules.then: Export CSV's visible/disabled state is derived from the same role/permission data source already used for the adjacent 'Add work item' button
business_rules.notes: Prevents permission-check drift between two adjacent toolbar actions over time.

business_rules.title: Submitted export request always reflects the current view state
business_rules.rule: The rich_filters payload sent to the server must be built from the view's live filter/project/sort state at the moment of the click, not a stale or default snapshot
business_rules.when: The user clicks Export CSV on the Issues List toolbar
business_rules.then: The request always includes provider='csv' and a rich_filters object matching what is currently rendered on screen, and a queued-confirmation toast is shown immediately after the request is accepted
business_rules.notes: Ensures the exported file always matches what the user visually confirmed before clicking Export, per the ideation's core promise ('exports exactly what's on screen').

business_rules.title: Polling terminates on a terminal job status, never spins forever
business_rules.rule: Polling for a specific job must stop once that job reaches a terminal status (completed or failed) — it must never continue polling indefinitely past a terminal state
business_rules.when: A submitted export job is being polled via the existing PrevExports interval mechanism
business_rules.then: On status=completed the UI shows a download action; on status=failed the UI shows a distinct failure indication; in both cases polling for that specific job ends
business_rules.notes: Reuses PrevExports' existing status===processing interval-clearing behavior; extends it to explicitly surface the failed terminal case rather than leaving it indistinguishable from processing.

api_contracts.description: Extends the existing ExportIssuesEndpoint with an optional rich_filters payload that scopes the export to the Issues List view's active filter/sort state. All existing behavior (provider, permissions, ExporterHistory lifecycle) is unchanged when rich_filters is omitted.

body.message: Once the export is ready you will be able to download it

response_errors.condition: rich_filters contains an unrecognized filter key
requesting user's role fails the existing WORKSPACE-level ROLE.ADMIN/ROLE.MEMBER check

api_contracts.notes: Existing endpoint: apps/api/plane/app/views/exporter/base.py:18-79. Extension point: rich_filters is the existing-but-unused ExporterHistory.rich_filters field, now actually populated and applied.

decisions.title: Extend the existing ExportIssuesEndpoint via rich_filters rather than build a new endpoint
decisions.rationale: Wiring the Issues List view's active filter/sort state through the existing rich_filters field (instead of a new independent endpoint) reuses working, tested infrastructure — permission scoping, Celery job lifecycle, signed-URL generation, and the CSV serializer — for the cost of one new server-side filter-application/validation path, rather than duplicating the entire export pipeline.
decisions.context: Refinement investigation of the actual Plane fork found a complete, working CSV/XLSX/JSON export pipeline already exists (ExportIssuesEndpoint, issue_export_task, ExporterHistory, presigned S3/MinIO URLs), including an unused rich_filters JSONField on ExporterHistory and a stubbed-out WorkspaceLevelWorkItemFiltersHOC block in ExportForm — clear evidence Plane's own team scaffolded this exact extension point but never wired it up.
alternatives_considered: A wholly separate view-scoped endpoint (GET /projects/<id>/issues/export/) independent of ExportIssuesEndpoint — rejected: duplicates permission scoping, Celery task, and signed-URL logic that already exists and works, for no functional benefit.

A new synchronous fast-path for small exports — rejected: diverges from the app's one established async-export convention; a small filtered export still completes within the existing 3-second polling interval.
decisions.notes: Formalizes the refinement's superseding decisions (see refinement 1c15a9e3, decisions list) as a spec-level Decision entity for the coverage gate.

breakdown_completeness.justification: Every FR, TR, BR, the API contract, and the Decision is linked to at least one of the 4 cards (Backend, Frontend, 2 Test cards) — verified via the validated spec's linked_task_ids on every structured entity. Backend card owns the server-side FRs/TRs/BRs/contract/decision; Frontend card owns the client-side FRs/TRs/BRs; the two Test cards partition all 6 test scenarios (3 backend-focused, 3 frontend-focused) with no scenario uncovered. No FR, TR, or AC is orphaned from a card.

granularity.justification: Backend and Frontend cards are each independently executable units of work (one Django/Celery change, one React component change) sized for a single agent session; splitting further (e.g. per-FR cards) would fragment a cohesive endpoint change for no execution benefit. Test cards are split backend/frontend to match the two implementation cards and stay within the board's max_scenarios_per_card=3 limit.

dependency_coherence.justification: Frontend card depends on Backend card (the frontend calls the contract the backend implements — real execution-order dependency, now recorded). Backend-test card depends on Backend card; Frontend-test card depends on Frontend card (tests need their implementation to exist first). No circular dependencies; the graph is a straightforward two-level fan-out matching the doc's intended Backend→Frontend(→handoff) sequencing.

test_coverage_quality.justification: All 6 test scenarios have concrete Given/When/Then with observable outcomes (exact HTTP status codes, exact CSV contents, exact UI state). Coverage includes the happy path (filter respected), two negative/edge paths (permission denial, invalid filter key), both terminal async states (completed, failed), and an explicit backward-compatibility regression scenario — a materially broader set than happy-path-only coverage.

evaluations.overall_justification: The spec is ready for execution: every requirement traces to a card, every acceptance criterion traces to a test scenario and a test card, the implementation strategy is grounded in real codebase citations rather than assumption, dependencies are explicit and acyclic, and the one prior ambiguity residue (illustrative vs. exhaustive rich_filters schema) is non-blocking per the validation gate's own finding. No FR/TR/AC is unaddressed by any card.

cards.title: Backend: wire rich_filters into ExportIssuesEndpoint / issue_export_task
Frontend: Export CSV action on Issues List toolbar
Test: frontend permission gating + polling UX

sprints.title: CSV export — filter-aware exporter extension
sprints.objective: Wire the existing ExportIssuesEndpoint/issue_export_task to the Issues List view's active filters via rich_filters, and add the Export CSV toolbar action, per the validated spec.
sprints.expected_outcome: Both implementation cards and both test cards done; validator confirms real evidence (test run output + a real export screenshot) against the spec's acceptance criteria; Nexus handoff artifact (the API contract) matches what the frontend actually implemented against.

screen_mockups.title: Issues List — Export action (sync + async states)
screen_mockups.description: Export action on the Issues List toolbar. Filter-aware: exports exactly the issues currently matching the active filters/sort. Three states resolved via ideation Q&A: idle (button), sync download (<500 matched issues — immediate file download, brief spinner), and async queued (>=500 matched issues — toast + progress state, polling for the signed link, then a download prompt; link valid 24h).

Issues List — toolbar (existing filters/sort applied)

Filters: Status = In Progress Sort: Priority ↓
State A — Sync (< 500 matched issues)

State B — Async (>= 500 matched issues)
Click "Export CSV" → toast: "Preparing export of 1,240 issues…" with a progress indicator → client polls job status → toast updates to "Export ready" with a Download button (signed link, valid 24h).

The ExporterHistory row persists the submitted `rich_filters` verbatim in its existing `rich_filters` JSONField for audit/replay, using the field that already exists on the model but is currently never populated.

The Issues List toolbar (IssuesHeader component, Header.RightItem section) renders an 'Export CSV' action, visible only to a user whose role satisfies the existing exporter's WORKSPACE-level role check (ROLE.ADMIN or ROLE.MEMBER).

Clicking the Export CSV action submits a POST to /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ with provider='csv' and a `rich_filters` payload built from the current Issues List view's active project, filter, and sort state.
On submission, the frontend shows a toast confirming the export was queued, reusing the existing ExportForm success-toast pattern (@plane/propel/toast).
The frontend polls the ExporterHistory list via the existing PrevExports interval mechanism and surfaces a download action once the matching entry's status becomes 'completed'.
If the matching export job's status becomes 'failed', the frontend surfaces the failure via a distinct error/toast state rather than continuing to poll indefinitely.

technical_requirements.text: `rich_filters` MUST be validated server-side against the same filter vocabulary as `IssueFilterSet` (apps/api/plane/utils/filters/filterset.py) — an unrecognized filter key is rejected with HTTP 400, never silently ignored, to prevent a silently-wrong export.

`issue_export_task` MUST apply `rich_filters` via the same ComplexFilterBackend/`IssueFilterSet`-compatible queryset construction already used by `IssueListEndpoint` (apps/api/plane/app/views/issue/base.py:80-205) — not a parallel/duplicate filter implementation — so filter semantics never drift between the live Issues List view and its export.

The existing membership/role scoping already present in `issue_export_task` (project__project_projectmember__member=..., is_active=True) remains the outer bound on every export: `rich_filters` may narrow the exported set but must never be capable of expanding it beyond what the requesting user's role can already view.

No change to `upload_to_s3`'s presigned-URL expiry (7 days, export_task.py:47,75-79,108-112) or to `IssueExportSerializer`'s field set (apps/api/plane/utils/porters/serializers/issue.py:12-63+) — per the refinement's superseding decision, this feature only adds filter application to the existing pipeline, not new serialization or storage code.

The Export button's visible/disabled state on the frontend MUST be derived from the same role/permission data the Issues List toolbar already uses for the adjacent 'Add work item' button (apps/web/core/components/issues/header.tsx:107-127) — not a new, separately-maintained permission check.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an Issues List view with an active filter (e.g. status = In Progress) and a chosen sort order, when the user clicks Export CSV, then the downloaded CSV contains only issues matching that filter, in the chosen sort order, and contains zero issues outside the filter.
Given a user whose role has no view access to a project's issues, when that project's Issues List is rendered, then the Export CSV action is not rendered or is disabled for that project.

Given a rich_filters payload containing an unrecognized filter key, when the export request is submitted, then the server responds HTTP 400 with a structured error identifying the invalid key, and no ExporterHistory row transitions past 'queued'.

Given an export job that reaches status='completed', when the frontend's next poll observes it, then the UI displays a working download action that resolves to the CSV via the existing 7-day presigned URL.
Given an export job that reaches status='failed', when the frontend's next poll observes it, then the UI displays a failure indication visibly distinct from the in-progress/polling state.

Given a request to POST /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ with no rich_filters field (a legacy caller), when processed, then the endpoint's behavior is identical to its pre-feature behavior (full workspace export, no regression).

test_scenarios.title: Export respects active filter and sort
test_scenarios.given: A project with 10 issues, 4 of which have priority=urgent, and an Issues List view with filter priority=urgent and sort=-created_at active
test_scenarios.then: The completed export's CSV contains exactly the 4 urgent issues, ordered by created_at descending, and zero non-urgent issues

test_scenarios.title: Export action hidden for a role without view access
test_scenarios.given: A user whose workspace role does not satisfy ROLE.ADMIN or ROLE.MEMBER for the target project
test_scenarios.when: That user's Issues List view for the project is rendered
test_scenarios.then: The Export CSV action is not present in Header.RightItem (or is rendered disabled), matching the visibility of the existing 'Add work item' button

test_scenarios.title: Unrecognized filter key rejects the request
test_scenarios.given: A POST to /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ with rich_filters.filters containing the key "not_a_real_filter"
test_scenarios.then: The server responds HTTP 400 with error=invalid_filter_key naming "not_a_real_filter", and no ExporterHistory row advances past status=queued for this request

test_scenarios.title: Completed export surfaces a working download link
test_scenarios.given: An export job in status=processing that the frontend is polling via the existing PrevExports interval
test_scenarios.when: The job transitions to status=completed with a presigned url set
test_scenarios.then: The next poll surfaces a download action in the UI, and following it downloads the CSV via the presigned URL before its 7-day expiry

test_scenarios.title: Failed export surfaces a distinct error state
test_scenarios.given: An export job in status=processing that the frontend is polling
test_scenarios.then: The next poll surfaces a failure indication in the UI that is visually and textually distinct from the processing/spinner state, and polling for that job stops

test_scenarios.title: Legacy request without rich_filters is unaffected
test_scenarios.given: The existing workspace-level ExportForm submits a POST to /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ with no rich_filters field, exactly as it does today
test_scenarios.when: The request is processed by the modified endpoint and issue_export_task
test_scenarios.then: The resulting export contains the full workspace issue set exactly as it would have before this feature shipped — no regression

business_rules.title: rich_filters can only narrow the exported set, never widen it
business_rules.rule: The exported issue set after applying rich_filters must always be a subset of the issues the requesting user's role already has view access to, computed by the existing membership/role scoping in issue_export_task
business_rules.when: A request to POST /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ includes a rich_filters payload
business_rules.then: issue_export_task applies rich_filters as an additional AND-ed constraint on top of the existing role-scoped queryset, never as a replacement for it or an independent filter that could bypass role scoping
business_rules.notes: Prevents a maliciously or accidentally crafted rich_filters payload from exporting issues the user cannot otherwise see. Source: apps/api/plane/bgtasks/export_task.py existing role-scoping queryset.

business_rules.title: Unknown filter keys reject the request rather than degrading silently
business_rules.rule: The server must not silently drop, ignore, or apply a best-effort interpretation of an unrecognized filter key
business_rules.when: rich_filters contains one or more keys that are not part of the IssueFilterSet-compatible filter vocabulary
business_rules.then: The endpoint responds HTTP 400 with a structured error identifying the invalid key(s), and no ExporterHistory row is created or advances past queued for that request
business_rules.notes: A silently-ignored filter key would produce an export that looks correct but is silently wrong (exports more than the user intended) — fail closed instead.

business_rules.title: Omitting rich_filters is fully backward compatible
business_rules.rule: The absence of rich_filters must never be interpreted as an empty/zero-match filter
business_rules.when: A request to POST /api/workspaces/<slug>/export-issues/ has no rich_filters field at all (legacy caller / existing ExportForm workspace-level export)
business_rules.then: The endpoint and issue_export_task behave exactly as they did before this feature — full workspace export, no behavioral regression for existing callers
business_rules.notes: Protects the existing ExportForm workspace-level export flow, which will continue calling this endpoint without rich_filters.

business_rules.title: Export button visibility mirrors the existing 'Add work item' permission check
business_rules.rule: The Export CSV action must not introduce a second, independently-maintained permission check that could drift from the existing role check
business_rules.when: The Issues List toolbar (Header.RightItem) is rendered for a given user and project
business_rules.then: Export CSV's visible/disabled state is derived from the same role/permission data source already used for the adjacent 'Add work item' button
business_rules.notes: Prevents permission-check drift between two adjacent toolbar actions over time.

business_rules.title: Submitted export request always reflects the current view state
business_rules.rule: The rich_filters payload sent to the server must be built from the view's live filter/project/sort state at the moment of the click, not a stale or default snapshot
business_rules.when: The user clicks Export CSV on the Issues List toolbar
business_rules.then: The request always includes provider='csv' and a rich_filters object matching what is currently rendered on screen, and a queued-confirmation toast is shown immediately after the request is accepted
business_rules.notes: Ensures the exported file always matches what the user visually confirmed before clicking Export, per the ideation's core promise ('exports exactly what's on screen').

business_rules.title: Polling terminates on a terminal job status, never spins forever
business_rules.rule: Polling for a specific job must stop once that job reaches a terminal status (completed or failed) — it must never continue polling indefinitely past a terminal state
business_rules.when: A submitted export job is being polled via the existing PrevExports interval mechanism
business_rules.then: On status=completed the UI shows a download action; on status=failed the UI shows a distinct failure indication; in both cases polling for that specific job ends
business_rules.notes: Reuses PrevExports' existing status===processing interval-clearing behavior; extends it to explicitly surface the failed terminal case rather than leaving it indistinguishable from processing.

api_contracts.description: Extends the existing ExportIssuesEndpoint with an optional rich_filters payload that scopes the export to the Issues List view's active filter/sort state. All existing behavior (provider, permissions, ExporterHistory lifecycle) is unchanged when rich_filters is omitted.

body.message: Once the export is ready you will be able to download it

response_errors.condition: rich_filters contains an unrecognized filter key
requesting user's role fails the existing WORKSPACE-level ROLE.ADMIN/ROLE.MEMBER check

api_contracts.notes: Existing endpoint: apps/api/plane/app/views/exporter/base.py:18-79. Extension point: rich_filters is the existing-but-unused ExporterHistory.rich_filters field, now actually populated and applied.

decisions.title: Extend the existing ExportIssuesEndpoint via rich_filters rather than build a new endpoint
decisions.rationale: Wiring the Issues List view's active filter/sort state through the existing rich_filters field (instead of a new independent endpoint) reuses working, tested infrastructure — permission scoping, Celery job lifecycle, signed-URL generation, and the CSV serializer — for the cost of one new server-side filter-application/validation path, rather than duplicating the entire export pipeline.
decisions.context: Refinement investigation of the actual Plane fork found a complete, working CSV/XLSX/JSON export pipeline already exists (ExportIssuesEndpoint, issue_export_task, ExporterHistory, presigned S3/MinIO URLs), including an unused rich_filters JSONField on ExporterHistory and a stubbed-out WorkspaceLevelWorkItemFiltersHOC block in ExportForm — clear evidence Plane's own team scaffolded this exact extension point but never wired it up.
alternatives_considered: A wholly separate view-scoped endpoint (GET /projects/<id>/issues/export/) independent of ExportIssuesEndpoint — rejected: duplicates permission scoping, Celery task, and signed-URL logic that already exists and works, for no functional benefit.

A new synchronous fast-path for small exports — rejected: diverges from the app's one established async-export convention; a small filtered export still completes within the existing 3-second polling interval.
decisions.notes: Formalizes the refinement's superseding decisions (see refinement 1c15a9e3, decisions list) as a spec-level Decision entity for the coverage gate.

screen_mockups.title: Issues List — Export action (sync + async states)
screen_mockups.description: Export action on the Issues List toolbar. Filter-aware: exports exactly the issues currently matching the active filters/sort. Three states resolved via ideation Q&A: idle (button), sync download (<500 matched issues — immediate file download, brief spinner), and async queued (>=500 matched issues — toast + progress state, polling for the signed link, then a download prompt; link valid 24h).
screen_mockups.html_content:
Issues List — toolbar (existing filters/sort applied)

Filters: Status = In Progress Sort: Priority ↓
State A — Sync (< 500 matched issues)
Click "Export CSV" → brief spinner on the button → browser download starts immediately (issues_export_2026-09-02.csv).
State B — Async (>= 500 matched issues)
Click "Export CSV" → toast: "Preparing export of 1,240 issues…" with a progress indicator → client polls job status → toast updates to "Export ready" with a Download button (signed link, valid 24h).
Export action is hidden/disabled for a user with no view access to the project's issues (permission-gated, matches existing project member view checks).

Nothing here changes system topology or introduces a new service boundary that would warrant an Architecture Design.
